messages:
maria: forwarding a customer report — they invited an external collaborator (email: j.smith@acme.com) and in the collaborators list they see the role, but clicking into the project console yields a 403. customer says: "I can see my role in the team list but whenever I try to open the project it shows 'Permission denied'"

alex: do we have their user id or an example session token? any repro steps from the customer?

maria: they pasted screenshots and said they logged in via Okta SSO. They accepted the invite, console shows them as 'Viewer (external)'. This started after we rolled out the org-label cleanup last week.

samir: ok i'll check rolebindings quickly. running lookup: 

```
redwoodctl iam list-bindings --project acme-prod --format=json | jq '.bindings[] | select(.principal=="j.smith@acme.com")'
```

samir: output looks weird — there are TWO bindings: one for "j.smith@acme.com" and another for "J.Smith@acme.com" (same email different case) and the latter is attached to a legacy external-guest identity that has an inherited deny tag from a previous org label.

alex: ah that smells like case-normalization drift between our SCIM sync and the Console. Did SCIM recently change capitalization rules?

scim-bot: SCIM sync completed for acme-okta at 3821012000, changes: group rename `acme-External` -> `external_collab`. No case-normalization flag set.

samir: root cause: when user accepted invite earlier we created a principal with lowercased email; after Okta resync the SCIM connector provisioned another principal preserving original capitalization. Console prefers the uppercase principal for UI display but our auth engine resolves the lowercase entry which was moved to a deprecated role-binding with an explicit deny tag (from old org-label cleanup). net result: UI shows role (from uppercase principal) but auth decision picks the lowercase principal's deny.

alex: can we confirm by querying policy evaluation for that session?

```
redwoodctl auth eval --principal "j.smith@acme.com" --resource "project:acme-prod" --session 3821012360
```

samir: eval shows DENY with a matched policy id: pol-legacy-inherit-213 (deny). If I run eval for "J.Smith@acme.com" it shows ALLOW.

maria: customer-facing workaround requested. They need access now.

samir: short-term fix: reattach the allowed principal and remove the deprecated binding. running: 

```
# promote canonical principal and remove orphaned deny binding
redwoodctl iam detach-binding --project acme-prod --principal "j.smith@acme.com" --binding pol-legacy-inherit-213
redwoodctl iam attach-binding --project acme-prod --principal "J.Smith@acme.com" --role Viewer
```

samir: done — please ask customer to sign out and sign back in. I also cleared SCIM cache for acme-okta.

maria: sent instructions to customer, asked them to confirm after re-login.

customer-reported (via email, pasted by maria): "I signed out and back in — can access the project now, thanks!" :tada:

alex: long-term we should normalize emails at provisioning or dedupe principals during SCIM sync. I'll open a tracker.

samir: created internal followup: ENG-priv-748 dedupe/scim-case-normalization, adding a migration that merges principals where lowercase(email) collisions exist and preserves the most recent allowed binding.

maria: reassigning to alex for the followup. closing this thread once ENG ticket is scheduled. :white_check_mark:
